lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create two HUD columns of 30px each (for score and health).

Make sure to pick grid-template-columns followed by : and then 30, px, 30, px, ;.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create four UI columns sized 30px 40px 50px 60px (icons).

Make sure to type 30px 40px 50px 60px.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this code?

The HUD item should be inside the HUD containerThere should be multiple HUD containersThere should be fewer HUD items

The HUD item should be inside the HUD container.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which property should we use to transform an element into a grid?

The display propertyThe grid-template-columns propertyThe position property

The display property.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
How many UI columns will be created when we use grid-template-columns: 40px 60px 40px on a game HUD container?

ThreeTwoFour

Make sure to pick Three.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create two equal HUD columns using pixel values.

Make sure to pick grid-template-columns, followed by 100px, and finally 100px.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens to an additional fifth HUD element in a two-column grid?

It's sent to the next row, the third row in this caseIt remains on the same rowIt overlaps the fourth item

It's sent to the next row, the third row in this case.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we create columns using the following code?

The space available is evenly distributed across all the columnsThe remaining space is evenly distributed across the first two columnsThe remaining space is evenly distributed across the last two columns

The space available is evenly distributed across all the columns.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create three equally sized UI columns.

Make sure to pick 30%, followed by 30%, and finally 30%.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the repeat() function to create four equally sized UI columns of 1fr width.

Make sure to pick repeat followed by ( and then 4, ,, 1fr, ).

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the repeat() function to create two HUD rows set to auto.

Make sure to type repeat(2, auto).

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
How many grid rows are defined in the HUD container?

Five grid rowsFour grid rowsSix grid rows

Five grid rows.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Keeping in mind that the HUD container doesn't have a height set, what does this code display?

Two rows that are only as tall as their contentA small row followed by a tall rowThree rows of equal size

Two rows that are only as tall as their content.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create two HUD rows using 60px 60px.

Make sure to pick 60px, followed by 60px.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
How many HUD elements does this container have?

Four grid itemsThree grid itemsFive grid items

Four grid items.
